description:
FOUND s502e (Opus, 2026-10-04) while shipping #2538 (Scalar::Util::set_prototype made real).  PRE-EXISTING on main e5d72352 and independent of #2538 (Sub::Util::set_prototype has the same gap).

REPRODUCER (scratch/s502e/p/sp2.pl in the s502e worktree; perl 5.40.3 first, PCL second):
    sub sp { scalar(@_) }
    my @l = (1, 2, 3);
    BEGIN { require Scalar::Util; Scalar::Util::set_prototype(\&sp, q($$)); }
    print "c ", sp(@l, 5), "\n";          # perl: c 2     PCL: c 4
    print "e ", eval q{ sp(@l, 5) }, "\n"; # perl: e 2     PCL: e 4

MECHANISM: PCL's prototype CONSUMPTION is a transpile-time fact (Pl::Environment's prototype table, filled from definitions and `use` merges); the run-time registry `%pcl-sub-prototypes` that set_prototype writes is read only by `prototype()`.  So a prototype installed at BEGIN time never reaches the parse of later statements, and a string eval (compiled at run time by the pl2cl server) does not consult the registry either.  prototype(\&sp) does answer '$$' (#2538).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT for a fix: does the string-eval compile path receive any run-time prototype facts today?  grep the eval request builder in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp for what it sends besides the capture alist; if nothing, the eval half needs the registry's (name -> text) pairs for subs visible in the eval's package sent with the request (the same channel the capture names ride, #296-B1), and the file-level half needs BEGIN-time evaluation feeding the transpiler -- which PCL does not have (the compile phase runs after transpile).  The eval half is the reachable one.

POPULATION: rare in practice (set_prototype at BEGIN then a bareword call relying on it); recorded as residue (3) of the not-supported.md "prototype()" entry.


ADDED 2026-10-06 (Fable, from the PerlMonks 44722 probes, task #2774): the same family without set_prototype -- a sub DEFINED by a string eval in BEGIN.  `BEGIN { eval q{sub zzz () { 42 }} } print zzz / 2` prints 21 in perl and 0 in PCL (the name is not known when the file is parsed, so `zzz` in operator position is the string "zzz"; silent).  `BEGIN { *zzz = sub () { 42 } }` IS seen and prints 21; `zzz /foo/` with an eval-defined arg-taking sub is also right (unknown word + `/.../` is repaired to a call with a match).

ADDED same day: brian d foy's example from the same reddit thread -- `BEGIN { my $subname = 'do_it'; *{$subname} = COND ? sub ($) { "A: $_[0]" } : sub ($$) { "B: $_[0] \U$_[1]" }; }  say do_it 'a', 'b';` -- perl prints `A: ab` or `B: a B`; PCL is right in the ($$) branch and prints `A: a` in the ($) branch (both arguments go to do_it).  His `print rand 5, sin 4, rand sin 1, 2, 3;` is identical to perl.
subject: A prototype set at RUN time (Scalar/Sub::Util::set_prototype in BEGIN) is reported by prototype() but never changes how later calls parse -- incl. a string eval compiled after the set (perl sp(@l,5) passes 2 args, PCL 4)
